info.title: SiteQwality API
info.description: Public REST API for SiteQwality: uptime monitoring, observability, incidents, and status pages.

get.summary: OAuth2 authorization server metadata (RFC 8414).
List API keys for the authenticated account.
get.description:
Secrets are never returned: only the stored prefix/suffix fragments, the
key type, any scopes, and the lifecycle timestamps. Revoked keys are
omitted; expired ones are included so the customer can see why a key
stopped working rather than watching it silently disappear.

The response stays a bare array, unchanged in shape from before hashing,
so a dashboard build that predates this deploy still renders the list.

post.summary: Create a new API key for the authenticated account.
post.description:
The response contains the full secret. This is the ONLY time it is ever
shown: only its SHA-256 is stored, so it cannot be retrieved again, only
rotated.

`key_type` defaults to `full` when omitted, which is exactly what every
key did before this endpoint grew types. The dashboard sends `ingest`
explicitly, because a key destined for a log-forwarder config should not
also be able to delete monitors.

200.description: Newly minted API key; the secret is only returned once

400.description: Invalid name, scopes or expiry, or key cap reached

delete.description:
The route and verb are unchanged, so the dashboard's existing delete
button keeps working, but the row is now kept and stamped `revoked_at`
instead of being deleted. Revocation takes effect immediately: both the
customer API and the ingest authorizers check `revoked_at` on every
request. Keeping the row preserves the audit history of a credential that
may have been used to change things.

Revoked keys disappear from `GET /account/api_key`, which is exactly what
a delete looked like before.

Deliberately idempotent: an unknown or already-revoked id still returns
200. The M2M equivalent 404s on an unknown id, but this endpoint has
always returned 200 for one (the DELETE simply matched no rows), and a
caller that has been relying on that must not start seeing errors.

post.summary:
Rotate an API key: mint a replacement and revoke the predecessor, in one
transaction.
post.description:
Because the secret is hashed at rest there is no "reveal it again", so
rotation is how a customer recovers from a lost or leaked key. The new key
inherits the old one's name, type, scopes, and expiry, so a rotated
credential drops straight into the same config slot.

The old secret stops working the moment this returns; there is no grace
period. A caller that needs overlap should instead create a second key,
deploy it, then revoke the first.

200.description: New key; the secret is only returned once

404.description: API key not found or already revoked

get.summary:
Customer-facing audit log: every mutating API request on the account with
its actor (user session, M2M client, API key, or impersonating staff),
newest first. Reads are capped to the last 90 days. Super admin, admin,
or auditor role required, since the log exposes other members' actions
and request IPs; audit read is the whole point of the auditor role
(Datadog's Audit Trail Read is the precedent).

One filtered, sorted, paged view of every monitor on the account: HTTP
checks, heartbeats and browser checks together.
get.description:
`total` is the size of the whole filtered set, not the length of `items`.

This exists because the three monitor types cannot be paged separately and
merged in the client. `GET /monitors/list` applies `limit` and `offset` to
`http_jobs` and `cron_jobs` independently, so `limit=10` can return twenty
rows and one offset means two different things; browser checks were not in
that endpoint at all and were merged in from an unfiltered list. A client
asking for "the next page" of the combined array therefore asked for an
offset that existed in none of the three sources, got nothing back, and
concluded there was no more data while monitors it had never shown sat in
the gap.

`/monitors/list` is unchanged: it is a documented public API surface.

post.summary: Response-time samples for a whole page of monitors, keyed by monitor id.
post.description:
The dashboard drew one sparkline per row and fetched each one with its own
`GET /http/job/{id}/recent`. A fifty-row page was fifty requests, roughly
half of them heartbeat and browser-check ids sent to an HTTP-job endpoint
that could only ever answer with an empty array, each one having taken a
reader connection to say so. At five hundred monitors that is a
self-inflicted outage.

Ids that are not HTTP monitors, or that belong to another account, are
absent from the response rather than present-and-empty. The caller reads
the map by id and treats a missing key as "no series", which is exactly
what a heartbeat or a browser check has.

200.description: Response-time samples keyed by monitor id

400.description: Too many monitor ids in one request

get.summary: A branded uptime report for one calendar month, as a printable page.
get.description:
Returns **HTML, not JSON**. The page is styled for paper: open it in a
browser and use Print, or "Save as PDF", to produce the document you send
on. There is a print button on the page for exactly that.

`month` is a UTC calendar month, `YYYY-MM`. Omit it and you get the last
complete month, which is the one a monthly report normally covers. Asking
for the month in progress is allowed and the report says plainly that it
is not finished.

The page takes its logo, colours and title from your status page branding.
An account with no branding gets a plain, unbranded document rather than
ours, because this is a report you hand to somebody else.

Two things the report states about itself, and worth knowing before you
send it:

* It covers **HTTP monitors only**. Heartbeat monitors and browser checks
  have no daily uptime figure behind them, so they are named as excluded
  rather than quietly dropped.
* Uptime comes from a rollup rebuilt daily at 03:00 UTC, so a report for
  the current month is month-to-date. The outage log is separate and is
  current to the minute.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: UTC calendar month as YYYY-MM (default: last complete month)

get.summary: List the calling partner's managed client accounts.
get.description:
Unpaged, deliberately. The partner SKU is sold per client and the largest
tier discussed is 50, so a partner's whole client list is one small page;
adding a pager would be inventing a problem. If a partner ever holds
hundreds of clients this becomes a paged endpoint, with `total` carried the
way `GET /monitors` carries it.

Each row's monitor counts come from the same three tables and the same
state-aware predicates `GET /monitors/totals` uses, in one query for the
whole list rather than one per client.

403.description: Caller is not an admin, or the account is not in the partner program

post.summary: Create a managed client account under the calling partner.
post.description:
The client is a perfectly ordinary account with a parent pointer: it has
its own monitors, its own status pages, its own quotas and its own
notification routing, and the partner works in it through the
`X-SQ-Account` header. Three things make it not-ordinary, all decided here
rather than inside the shared provisioning seam:

* **No Stripe customer.** The partner is billed on one subscription; a
  client is never billed directly, so it never gets a customer object to
  leak or reconcile.
* **No welcome email.** The contact never asked us for an account. A
  "welcome to SiteQwality" email out of nowhere is the partner's
  relationship to manage, not ours.
* **A Stytch organization with no member and no session.** Nobody is
  signing in yet. The organization exists up front so the partner's later
  invite has somewhere to land, and the local user row (which the account
  needs, for `primary_user_id`) carries a NULL `stytch_member_id` until
  then.

delete.summary: Soft-delete one of the caller's client accounts.
delete.description:
Marks the client account deleted and nothing else. That single flag is what
every downstream consequence keys on, and each one is what removing a client
should mean:

* the client's own users lose access,
* the client's checks stop running,
* the client can no longer be opened with `X-SQ-Account`, and
* the client slot is freed immediately, so you can add a replacement.

The client's data is retained per the retention policy. **This is not an
erasure endpoint.** Suspension history is left intact.

403.description: Caller is not an admin, or the account is not in the partner program

404.description: No live client account of yours with that id

put.summary: Set one of the caller's client accounts to a named entitlement bundle.
put.description:
A partner picks a bundle, never individual packs: the wholesale rate is flat
per client, so what a client gets is one of the two compositions that rate
was priced against.

The bundle becomes ordinary subscription rows on the client account, so
quota metering, paid feature unlocks and every other downstream consequence
behave exactly as they do for a direct customer.

**Idempotent, and that is the intended way to use it.** Setting the bundle a
client is already on grants nothing, cancels nothing, and does not move a
billing anniversary, so a console that re-asserts state on every save is
safe.

Changing a client's bundle moves that client between the wholesale lines on
your own subscription, prorated for the remainder of the current period.

403.description: Caller is not an admin, or the account is not in the partner program

404.description: No live client account of yours with that id

422.description: Unknown bundle name, or no bundle in the body

get.summary: Per-product usage counters for one of the caller's client accounts.
get.description:
Resolved through exactly the path `/billing/usage` uses, against the
CLIENT's account id: `account_usage_periods` derives the window each
product is metered in, and `usage_counters_for_resolved_periods` reads each
product's counter from its own window. Nothing here may shortcut to a
single period string. A client can be anchored on a different day per
product, and reporting one period is what made the 2026-08-02 hard-stop
incident invisible for a month.

A client provisioned but not yet given an entitlement bundle has no paid
packs, so every product resolves to the calendar month and only the
products it has actually used carry a row.

AccountMonitorTotals.description:
Account-wide monitor totals with optional 24h aggregates.

The aggregate fields (uptime, response times, and their previous-24h
counterparts for trend deltas) are omitted from the JSON when no HTTP
performance data exists in the window.

by_type.description:
The same four counts split per monitor type.

Additive: the four fields above are unchanged, and still mean every
monitor type added together. This exists so a per-type counter tile
can read an account-wide number instead of counting the rows of one
page of the (paged) monitor list. Never omitted, and never partial.

uptime_24h.description: Aggregate uptime percentage across all HTTP checks over the last 24h.

avg_response_time_ms.description: Average HTTP response time (ms) over the last 24h.

p95_response_time_ms.description: 95th-percentile HTTP response time (ms) over the last 24h.

prev_uptime_24h.description: Aggregate uptime percentage for the previous 24h window (24-48h ago).

prev_avg_response_time_ms.description: Average HTTP response time (ms) for the previous 24h window.

prev_p95_response_time_ms.description: 95th-percentile HTTP response time (ms) for the previous 24h window.

AccountSlaMonitor.description: One monitor in the account SLA report.

breached_months.description: Number of months in the report window with `attained == false`.

months.description: Newest month first, aligned with the response's `months` labels.

default_target.description: Target applied when a monitor has none configured.

AcmValidationCname.description: The DNS records the customer must add to their DNS provider.

name.description:
The CNAME record name the customer must create, e.g.
"_abc123.status.theircompany.com"

value.description: The CNAME record value to point at, e.g. "xyz.acm-validations.aws"

url.description: Incoming webhook URL of the Google Chat space.
Incoming webhook URL of the Mattermost channel.

api_key.description: Alerts API key of the OpsGenie API integration.

routing_key.description: Events API v2 routing key (integration key) of the PagerDuty service.

app_token.description: API token of the Pushover application.

ApiKeyStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a key, derived rather than stored so it can never
disagree with the timestamps.

ApiKeySummary.description:
One API key in list responses. Never contains the secret: after creation
the secret exists only in the customer's hands.

key_prefix.description: First 8 characters of the secret, kept in plaintext for display.

key_last_four.description: Last 4 characters of the secret, kept in plaintext for display.

ApiKeyType.description:
What a customer API key is allowed to do.

Mirrors the Datadog split between an API key (telemetry push) and an
application key (full API access), collapsed into one credential with a
type so the ingest path and the management path can share a table.

ApiKeyWithSecretResponse.description:
Response for create and rotate, the ONLY places a full secret ever
appears. It is not stored and cannot be retrieved again.

secret.description: The full secret. Shown exactly once; store it now.

ApiOpsGenieIntegrationDetails.description: The API key is a secret, so the API shape is empty.

ApiPagerDutyIntegrationDetails.description:
The routing key is a secret, so the API shape is empty (same treatment as
the Slack token).

ApiPushbulletIntegrationDetails.description: The access token is a secret, so the API shape is empty.

ApiPushoverIntegrationDetails.description: The user key and app token are secrets, so the API shape is empty.

AttentionItem.description: A single actionable item on the dashboard "Needs Attention" list.

title.description: One-line human-readable description rendered verbatim by the UI.

monitor_id.description: The monitor this item points at, when it concerns a single monitor.

monitor_name.description: Display name for the affected monitor or domain.

incident_id.description: The incident this item points at; incidents only.

created_at.description:
Reference instant for the item: when the incident started, when the
monitor went down, or when the cert/domain expires.

link.description: SPA-relative link to the detail page for this item.

AttentionItemType.description:
Discriminates the kinds of items the dashboard "Needs Attention" list can
surface, in priority order (incidents first, slow monitors last).

AttentionResponse.description:
Response for `GET /monitors/attention`. `items` is capped; `total_count`
reports how many qualified before the cap.

AuthMethodsResponse.description:
What auth methods are configured for a given email. Used by the email-first
login UI to branch between password, magic link, and OAuth.

exists.description: `true` if a local account exists for this email.

has_password.description: `true` if the account can authenticate with a password.

has_oauth_google.description: `true` if the account has Google OAuth linked.

has_passkey.description:
`true` if the account has a registered WebAuthn passkey.
Always `false` today, wired for the future passkey feature.

AuthResponse.description: Unified authentication response returned by login, signup, and refresh endpoints.

AuthorizationServerMetadata.description:
RFC 8414 authorization server metadata, served at
`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` so client libraries can
auto-configure instead of being handed a URL to paste.

response_types_supported.description:
Empty: this server issues no authorization codes and no tokens by
redirect. RFC 8414 still expects the key to be present.

body_bytes.description:
True size of the body in bytes, so a client can show it before the
download starts.

oneOf.description:
Omitted means `full`.

This is deliberately NOT the dashboard's default (which is `ingest`,
the safer choice). The API default has to preserve the historical
behaviour, because a customer script that has been POSTing
`{"friendly_name": "..."}` for years must keep getting a key that can
do what its keys have always done.

scopes.description:
Optional scope restriction for a `full` key. Omitted or empty means
unrestricted, which is how every existing key behaves. Must be drawn
from the same `read:<family>` / `write:<family>` taxonomy as M2M
clients. Rejected on an `ingest` key, which never reaches the scope
chokepoint at all.

expires_in_days.description:
Optional lifetime in days. Omitted means the key never expires, which
matches the Datadog model and is what every existing key does.

oneOf.description: Preferred HTTP version. Defaults to `auto` when omitted.

confirmation_threshold.description:
Number of consecutive failed checks (1-10) required before the monitor
is considered down and notifications are sent. Defaults to 1 (alert on
the first failed check).

name.description: Human-readable client name, e.g. "CI deploy hook".

scopes.description:
Granted scopes, e.g. `["read:monitors", "write:monitors"]`. Must be
non-empty and drawn from the documented scope taxonomy.

handoff_day.description:
Weekly layers only: weekday of the handoff, 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday,
interpreted together with `handoff_time` in the schedule's timezone.
Ignored for `daily` and `custom` rotations.

display_name.description:
The partner's label for this client, e.g. "Acme Corp". Not shown to the
client and not client-editable: it is how the partner console lists
them, and it names the client's Stytch organization.

contact_email.description:
The client's real contact address. It becomes the child account's
primary user and the address its default notification group alerts, so
an outage on the client's site reaches the client rather than the
partner.

Must be distinct across the partner's client accounts. See
`Database::partner_client_account_id_by_contact_email` for why that is
a pricing rule and not a data-hygiene preference.

contact_name.description: The contact's name, when the partner knows it. Absent is normal.

display_name.description: Label shown in the dashboard and at Stytch, e.g. "Okta".

email_domain.description:
Email domain to claim for SSO discovery, e.g. `corp.example.com`.
Optional at create; the connection is not startable from the login
screen until it is set AND the connection is active.

CustomerAuditActorType.description: Who performed an audited action. Mirrors `customer_audit_log.actor_type`.

CustomerAuditLogEntry.description:
One row in the customer audit-log list response. `request_ip` is
stringified for JSON transport (Postgres `INET` round-trips as
`IpNetwork`).

actor_api_key_id.description:
The API key that acted, when `actor_type` is `api_key`. Null on rows
written before attribution landed (2026-08-06).

actor_api_key_name.description:
The key's friendly name at read time (keys are revoked, never
deleted, so this resolves for historical rows too).

impersonated_by.description: Staff user id when the action was performed under impersonation.

actor_user_id.description: Only entries performed by this user.

actor_api_key_id.description: Only entries performed by this API key.

oneOf.description: Only entries with this actor type.

action.description:
Action name, matched exactly or as a dot-prefix: `http.job` also
matches `http.job.regions`, but never `http.jobs`.

target_kind.description: Only entries targeting this resource kind (first path segment).

target_id.description: Only entries targeting this resource id.

since.description: RFC3339; clamped to the read window.

read_window_days.description: Days of history the endpoint serves; older rows are not returned.

email_verified.description:
Whether the caller's Stytch member email is verified.
Magic-link and Google OAuth signups land verified; email + password
signups land unverified until the link in the welcome email is clicked.

mfa_enrolled.description: Whether the Stytch member has at least one MFA factor enrolled.

email.description: The email address Stytch has on file. Handy for the banner copy.

HourlyErrorRate.description: Error rate broken down by hour of day (0-23, UTC).

HttpJobHttpVersion.description:
Preferred HTTP version for the check transport (isahc/libcurl).
Stored on the job; observed negotiated version is on `http_job_results.http_version`.

target.description: Effective SLA target percentage applied to every month.

target_source.description:
Where the target came from: "status_page" when configured on a
status-page link (strictest wins), else "default".

auto_created.description:
True when the incident was opened automatically by a monitor state
change; false for incidents created manually.

template.description: Normalised message template, e.g. "Connection timeout to {IP}:{NUM} after {NUM}ms"

count.description: Total count of log entries matching this template in the query window

first_seen.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the earliest matching log in the window

last_seen.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent matching log in the window

samples.description: Up to 3 raw message samples from the matching logs

investigate_search.description:
Pre-built search term for the "Investigate" button: a short unique
substring extracted from the template (first non-placeholder token >= 4 chars)

token_endpoint.description: OAuth2 client_credentials token endpoint for this environment.

M2MClientSummary.description:
One M2M client in list responses. Never contains a secret; only the last
four characters Stytch retains for display.

client_id.description: Stytch client_id, the OAuth2 `client_id` used at the token endpoint.

M2MClientWithSecretResponse.description:
Response for create and rotate, the ONLY places a full secret appears.
The secret is never stored and can never be retrieved again.

client_secret.description: Full client secret. Shown exactly once; store it now.

token_endpoint.description: OAuth2 client_credentials token endpoint for this environment.

redirect_url.description:
SPA URL the Stytch email link should redirect to. The SPA reads the
`token` query param and POSTs it to `/auth/magic-link/authenticate`.
Defaults to `${base_frontend_url}/auth/magic-link/callback`.

sent.description:
Always `true` in the success path. Frontend uses this as a "check your
email" trigger. It does not leak whether the user exists.

MemberInfo.description: Full member info returned on every authentication response.

MetricHistogramBucket.description: One time bucket of aggregated histogram data.

total.description: Total number of observations in this time bucket.

sum.description: Sum of all observed values in this time bucket.

MetricHistogramParams.description: Query parameters for the histogram endpoint.

MetricHistogramResponse.description:
Histogram query response: per-time-bucket percentiles plus the raw
bucket-count matrix for heatmap rendering.

bounds.description:
Upper-bound labels for the histogram buckets, in ascending order.
The last entry may be "+Inf".

MetricQueryParams.description: Query parameters for the time-series chart endpoint.

MetricSummaryParams.description: Query parameters for the summary table endpoint.

MonitorTotalsByType.description:
Account-wide monitor counts split by monitor type.

All three keys are ALWAYS present, including for a type the account has
none of, which is why this is a struct and not a map. A dashboard tile
that reads a missing key renders nothing at all, and "nothing" reads as a
stuck loading state rather than as zero.

MonitorType.description:
Which table a unified monitor row came from.

The dashboard maps this straight onto the `_type` field its table and cell
renderers key off, and splits the page back into per-type slices with it.
It is the one field on the row that is never null.

MonitorTypeTotals.description:
The four monitor counts for one monitor type.

Same four numbers, same meaning, as the top level of
`AccountMonitorTotals`, restricted to a single type.

MonitorsPage.description: One server-filtered, server-sorted page of the unified monitor list.

total.description:
Number of monitors matching the filters, across every page. This is
what "X-Y of N" is built from; it is not the length of `items`.

provider.description: Provider identifier. Currently "google" (Branch C will add "github").

handoff_day.description:
Weekly layers only: weekday of the handoff, 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday,
interpreted together with `handoff_time` in the schedule's timezone.

pagerduty_severity.description:
Severity of trigger events sent through this notification. Defaults
to `critical` when the caller omits it.

PagerDutySeverity.description:
`payload.severity` on trigger events. The user picks this per
notification; DOWN alerts default to `critical`.

PartnerBundle.description:
The named entitlement presets a partner may set on a client account.

Presets rather than free choice of packs: the partner pays a flat
wholesale rate per client, so what a client gets has to be one of the two
things that rate was priced against. A partner who needs something else
buys it retail on the client account or talks to us.

PartnerBundlePackSummary.description: One pack the client holds after the bundle was applied.

clients.description:
Live clients only, newest first. A soft-deleted client is absent, which
matches the `X-SQ-Account` switch refusing to open one.

PartnerClientMonitorTotals.description:
Monitor counts for one client, in the same state-aware sense
`GET /monitors/totals` uses: a paused monitor counts in `total` and
`paused` and in neither `online` nor `down`.

PartnerClientProductUsage.description:
One product's counters for one client.

Field-for-field the shape `/billing/usage` returns, on purpose: a partner
reading a client's usage here and that client reading their own usage in
the dashboard must not see two different numbers or two different units.

current_usage.description:
Usage in the product's CUSTOMER-FACING unit (see `unit`), not the raw
tracking unit: synthetic is metered in seconds and reported in minutes.

period.description: The period THIS product is metered in.

PartnerClientSummary.description: One managed client account, as the console lists it and as create answers.

account_id.description:
The client's account id. This is the value the partner sends as
`X-SQ-Account` to open the client in the ordinary dashboard.

contact_email.description:
Nullable because `accounts.primary_user_id` carries no foreign key; see
`DbPartnerChildAccount::contact_email`.

suspended.description:
Convenience mirror of `suspended_at.is_some()`, so a client list can
render the badge without parsing a timestamp.

PartnerClientUsageResponse.description:
Response for `GET /partner/accounts/{id}/usage`.

Deliberately carries NO top-level period. `/billing/usage` still has one
for backwards compatibility, and it is a lie whenever an account is
anchored on a different day per product: reporting one is what made the
2026-08-02 hard-stop incident invisible for a month. A new endpoint gets to
start correct.

products.description:
Every product, including the ones with no counter row yet, is NOT
guaranteed here: this lists the counter rows that exist, exactly as
`/billing/usage` does. A product a client has never used has no row.

label.description:
Human label for the passkey (e.g., "iPhone 15 Pro"). Stored on Stytch
alongside the credential so users can identify their devices.

public_key_credential_creation_options.description:
Opaque JSON string. The browser passes this straight to
`navigator.credentials.create()` after parsing.

level.description: Comma-separated levels; defaults to "error,warn" when absent or empty.

limit.description: Max patterns to return; default 20, max 50.

messages_examined.description: Total distinct messages examined before clustering

logo_url.description: CDN URL, never an S3 key

RecentChecksBatchRequest.description: Request body for the batched sparkline endpoint.

monitor_ids.description:
Monitor ids to fetch response-time samples for. Ids that are not HTTP
monitors, or that belong to another account, are simply absent from
the response.

ResponseTimeDataPoint.description: One aggregate bucket on the dashboard response-time trends chart.

avg_ms.description: Average HTTP response time (ms) across all checks in the bucket.

p95_ms.description: 95th-percentile HTTP response time (ms) in the bucket.

ResponseTimeSeriesResponse.description:
Response for `GET /monitors/response-time-series`: the last 24h of
account-wide response-time aggregates in fixed-width buckets. Buckets
with no checks are absent rather than zero-filled.

interval_minutes.description: Width of each bucket in minutes.

since.description: The frontend sends `since` (start of range); `to` defaults to now.

has_frustration.description:
`true` keeps only sessions carrying at least one frustration signal
(rage + dead + error clicks summed). `false` and absent are the same
thing: no filter. Applied in SQL, so `total` stays the filtered set
size (unlike `has_replay`, see `list_rum_sessions`).

rage_click_count.description:
Frustration signals the SDK detects on click actions and stores in
`rum_events.frustration`. Always present, never null: a session with
none reports 0.

`serde(default)` is deserialization-side robustness only, so a
ClickHouse row missing the key cannot make `parse_lines` drop the whole
session (it swallows parse errors with `filter_map(...ok())`). The
serializer always emits these, so `schema(required = true)` keeps the
generated OpenAPI honest: without it utoipa infers optional from the
serde default and the published contract disagrees with the real one,
while the sibling `view_count` / `error_count` stay required.

action_count.description:
Total user actions in the session, summed from `rum_measures`.

Reads 0 for every session recorded so far: the browser SDK hardcodes
`action_count: 0` on the measures it emits. See the caveat on
`build_rum_sessions_list_query` in `common/src/db/rum_analytics.rs`.
Not rendered anywhere in the dashboard for that reason.

SamlConnectionResponse.description:
SAML connection as returned to the dashboard. Combines our row (account
linkage, claimed domain) with the live Stytch object (SP-side values the
customer pastes into the IdP, plus the configured IdP values).

status.description: `pending` until the IdP side is configured, then `active`.

acs_url.description: Service-provider values for the IdP side of the setup.

idp_entity_id.description: Configured IdP values (echoed back so the UI can show current state).

has_certificate.description: Whether at least one verification certificate is on file.

ScimConnectionResponse.description:
SCIM connection as returned to the dashboard. Never carries the bearer
token; only the last four characters.

base_url.description: SCIM base URL the customer pastes into their IdP.

ScimConnectionWithTokenResponse.description: Create / rotate response: carries the bearer token exactly once.

bearer_token.description: Full bearer token. Shown once, never stored, never retrievable again.

packs.description: The packs the bundle grants, with the catalog ids they resolved to.

granted.description:
How many partner-sourced entitlement rows this call created. Zero when
the client was already on the bundle, which is what makes the endpoint
safe to call repeatedly.

cancelled.description:
How many partner-sourced entitlement rows this call cancelled, i.e.
what the previous bundle had that this one does not. Rows sourced from
Stripe or from a staff grant are never counted here because they are
never touched.

SlaMonth.description: Attainment of one calendar month against the monitor's target.

month.description: "YYYY-MM" (UTC calendar month; the newest month is partial).

uptime_percentage.description:
Average of daily uptime percentages, 3 decimals. `null` when the
month has no check data.

attained.description: `uptime >= target`; `null` when there is no data to judge.

SsoAuthenticateRequest.description: Body for `POST /login/sso`, which completes the SSO redirect.

token.description:
The `token` query param Stytch appends to the login redirect URL when
`stytch_token_type=sso`.

SsoStartResponse.description:
Response for `POST /auth/sso/start`.

Enumeration-safe by construction: the shape is identical whether or not
the domain has SSO, and the status code is always 200. `redirect_url` is
`null` when there is no startable connection, which covers "no such
account", "account without SSO", and "SSO configured but not yet active"
with one indistinguishable answer.

redirect_url.description: Stytch SSO start URL to redirect the browser to, or `null`.

cname_target.description:
The intermediate CNAME the customer must point their domain at,
e.g. "<status_page_id>.custom.siteqwality.com"

acm_validation.description: ACM DNS validation records, needed while status = "pending_validation"

error.description:
One of the RFC 6749 error codes: `invalid_request`, `invalid_client`,
`invalid_scope`, `unsupported_grant_type`, `temporarily_unavailable`.

error_description.description:
Human-readable detail. Never distinguishes "unknown client" from
"wrong secret": both are `invalid_client` with the same description.

access_token.description: The bearer token to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

expires_in.description: Lifetime in seconds, passed through from the issuer.

scope.description: Space-delimited granted scopes. Absent when the token carries none.

totp_code.description: 6-digit code from the user's authenticator app.

qr_code_url.description: `otpauth://` URL, rendered as a QR code on the client.

recovery_codes.description: One-time recovery codes. Shown once; never recoverable.

tags.description: JSON-encoded span attribute filters, e.g. `{"http.method":"GET"}`.

p50_ms.description:
Trace duration percentiles for traces starting in this bucket (ms).
Zero when the bucket has no traces.

tags.description: JSON-encoded span attribute filters, e.g. `{"http.method":"GET"}`.

UnifiedMonitor.description:
One row of the unified monitor list.

Fields are emitted as explicit `null` rather than omitted when they do not
apply to the row's type. The dashboard reads several of them positionally
(an absent `method` and a null `method` are not the same thing to it), and
bulk edit spreads the whole row back into an update request, so a missing
key is a silently blanked setting rather than a cosmetic difference.

friendly_name.description:
Display name. Browser checks store this as `name`; it is projected here
so one column renderer serves all three types.

uptime_24h.description:
Uptime percentage over the last 24h. HTTP monitors only, and null when
the monitor has no checks in the window.

group_notifications.description: Notification groups, resolved in one batched query for the whole page.

timeout_ms.description:
Milliseconds. Browser checks store seconds; the value is converted so
the Timeout column reads true for them instead of blanking.

method.description:
Explicitly null for heartbeats and browser checks. The dashboard's
legacy "no method means heartbeat" heuristic still exists as a
fallback, so this must be present and null rather than omitted.

oneOf.description: Preferred HTTP version for the check client.

confirmation_threshold.description:
Number of consecutive failed checks (1-10) required before the monitor
is considered down and notifications are sent.

UpdateSamlConnectionRequest.description:
Body for `PUT /account/sso/saml/connection`. Every field is optional;
only supplied fields are forwarded to Stytch.

Two ways to configure the IdP side: paste a `metadata_url` (Stytch fetches
entity id, SSO URL, and certificate) or fill the three fields by hand.

clear_email_domain.description: Set true to release the claimed domain (disables SSO discovery).

x509_certificate.description: PEM-encoded X.509 signing certificate from the IdP.

sla_target_percentage.description: SLA target percentage (e.g. 99.9). Send null to clear.

role.description:
One of `admin`, `member`, `viewer`. `owner` is not assignable here:
ownership transfer is a separate operation.

bearer_auth.description: Generate an API key in account settings and pass it as `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>`.
